answer: Rate-limited issuance registry. (1) Each identity binds a hardware serial; the registry keeps a counter and a global nonce. (2) Each request carries the nonce and sender serial; the registry checks counter < limit and increments atomically, blocking duplicate serials. (3) Violators post a 500 POA bond; each slash takes 200 POA and freezes the identity 24 hours, with a randomness-beacon cross-check blocking fake nonces. (4) Cloning 5,000 identities costs 2,500,000 POA in bonds, then 5,000 days. A walnut prism on velvet — one bead per guest, bouncer throws out anyone wearing two.
